comments.body:
## HANDOFF to the Jira Server/DC session (epic e369)

Reparented here because this is a DC/reconciler-seam decision, not standalone. Summary of the
gap you now own:

**What is not implemented in production:** the `(inbound, probe)` dispatch chain — rebar's
mechanism to distinguish a **deleted** Jira issue from one that merely **aged out of the fetch
window** — has NO live producer. `differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes` only
emits when it sees `local_state[key]["jira_key"]`, but its sole production caller
(`run_differs.py:222`, `compute_mutations(ctx.prev_snapshot, ctx.curr_snapshot, ...)`) passes a
FETCHED Jira snapshot, whose entries are raw Jira `fields` dicts (`fetcher.py:479`, contract
`_snapshot_schema.py:96-135`) and carry no `jira_key`. So the loop never fires, and everything
downstream is dead in prod: `_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch` (run_differs.py),
`inbound_probe.py` (ProbeResult/ProbeBranch/router), `backend.probe_remote`, the
`SupportsAbsenceProbe` capability.

**What is not tested (and why the suite is still green):**
- The DC live cell that would exercise it — `test_a_deleted_dc_issue_never_plans_a_local_teardown`
  (Row 14, tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py) — is `@_skip`/`@_skip_no_extra`, so
  it only runs against a real DC with extras; it does not run in normal CI.
- Even when it runs, its oracle was CORRECTED (ticket b9b8): it NO LONGER asserts an
  `(inbound, probe)` entry (that citation was wrong/unsatisfiable). It now asserts the real
  ADR-0028 section-1 observable — deleting the DC issue must NOT plan a local teardown. So the
  probe path itself is verified NOWHERE.
- The only fixture that supplies a `jira_key`-bearing `local_state` is the unit test
  tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_emits_probe.py — a synthetic input the real
  caller never produces.

**Why it matters for DC:** ADR 0028 relies on the bounded direct GET->404 to PROVE deletion
(vs aged-out). Today, on DC, that discrimination is exercised only by the outbound differ's
bounded GET (`outbound_differ.py:692-702`), while the inbound-probe arm is inert.

**The decision you inherit (this ticket's AC #1): wire it or delete it.**
- WIRE: migrate the caller to pass a `jira_key`-bearing local_state AND — in the SAME change —
  remove `reconcile_helpers.drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions` (that suppression only
  exists because the caller passes the legacy prev/curr snapshot pair; migrating makes the
  suppressed emissions correct again — leaving both silently drops real work). Then un-skip /
  restore a DC cell that asserts the probe on a confirmed-deleted bound pair.
- DELETE: remove the dead chain (inbound_probe.py, the dispatch arm, the capability) and accept
  deletion detection stays solely on the outbound-GET path.

Full analysis and the "what is NOT the fix" warning are in this ticket's description. No code
has been changed for this ticket.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## DECISION-3B5F-A: **DELETE**. ADR 0028 para 2's discrimination IS implemented elsewhere — twice, both live. Plus a finding the brief did not have.

AC #1 asks whether the direct-GET confirmation "has since been implemented elsewhere". It has. Two
independent live implementations, both in the same pass as the dead arm:

### Citation 1 — `outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` (ADR 0028 L13)

`outbound_differ.py:142` maps `HTTPError.code == 404` → the `_DELETED` sentinel
(`outbound_differ.py:91`), consumed at `outbound_differ.py:693`. This is the bounded direct GET the
ADR's L13 names, and the ADR cites this very module (`outbound_differ.py:73-135,450-644`) as its home.

### Citation 2 — `binding_walk`, the ADR para 4 binding-driven loop

`binding_walk.py:187-196` performs the bounded GET for every off-snapshot binding and maps it to the
four-way state the ADR's Consequences describe:

    got is _DELETED         -> ObservedJira.CONFIRMED_404
    got is _TRANSPORT_ERROR -> ObservedJira.TRANSPORT_ERROR
    HTTP 200                -> ObservedJira.PRESENT (alive but out of window)
    client is None          -> ObservedJira.ABSENT_IN_WINDOW (defer, never deletion)

`classify.py:59` defines `CONFIRMED_404`; `classify.py:79` defines `RETIRE_AFTER_GRACE`. It reuses
`outbound_differ`'s sentinels **unchanged** (stated at `binding_walk.py:132`), and
`binding_walk.py:281-299` advances grace / retires **only** on `CONFIRMED_404`, with an explicit
"never on ABSENT_IN_WINDOW (ADR 0028 §2)".

**Both are live.** `run_differs.py:222` calls the dead `compute_mutations`; `run_differs.py:257` calls
`_run_differs_binding_walk` — same function, same pass.

### The ADR itself assigns this to the outbound side, which makes the inbound arm architecturally wrong

L16 shares a `200` overlay with the inbound differ but excludes `404`s and transport errors
**deliberately**, "so a gone issue is never inbound-mirrored (**retirement stays outbound-owned**)".
An `(inbound, probe)` arm whose whole purpose is to route a confirmed 404 into the inbound path
contradicts that ownership split. The chain is a vestige of the design L13/L16 replaced, not an
unfinished part of the current one.

### The finding the brief did not have: c244's same-pass re-create is ALSO dead

`route_inbound_probe` (`reconcile_helpers.py:296-334`) is the **sole** producer of `(inbound, delete)`
in the engine — verified by searching every `MutationAction.delete` construction: the only other one
is `run_differs.py:588`, which is `direction=outbound`. And `route_inbound_probe` takes an
`(inbound, probe)` Mutation as its input.

So with no `(inbound, probe)` producer: `route_inbound_probe` never runs → `(inbound, delete)` is never
produced → `_apply_inbound_delete` (`apply_inbound.py:175`) never runs → the
`create_after_hard_delete` follow-on (`apply_inbound.py:220`) is never emitted.

**That is an ADR-documented Consequence that is currently inert:** "Confirmed hard-delete of a
still-locally-present ticket now re-creates it (c244) … This closes the former `epic-3e36` gap where
the follow-on was built but never consumed." The follow-on is, once again, never consumed — for a
different reason than in `epic-3e36`.

I am recording this rather than letting DELETE quietly take it, because it is the one real cost of
deleting and it was not in the brief.

### Why it is still DELETE, and what is actually lost

The **outcome** survives; only the **immediacy** is lost. On a confirmed 404 `binding_walk` retires the
binding after grace (`note_absent_or_rekey`, `binding_walk.py:294-299`). Once retired, the local
ticket is unbound, and the normal unbound-local → outbound-create path re-creates the Jira issue.
So a hard-deleted issue whose local ticket is still present is re-created **eventually** (after grace),
where c244 promised **same-pass**.

WIRE would buy back that immediacy but at a bad price: it means migrating `run_differs` to pass real
local state AND removing `drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions`, which re-enables the snapshot
differ's `field_drift` and `unbound_local` arms (`reconcile_helpers.py:505-511`). Those arms now
**duplicate** work `outbound_differ` (local↔remote diff) and `binding_walk` (drift classes A and B)
already do — and `binding_walk.py:120-123` states the division of labour explicitly, skipping
`active_local_ids` because the field differ owns them. Re-lighting a legacy `(prev, curr)` arm to
recover one property, while it double-emits two others, is a worse change than restoring that property
where the 404 is already in hand.

**Follow-up filed** for restoring same-pass re-create inside `binding_walk` — a much smaller and
correctly-placed change, since `CONFIRMED_404` + the local ticket are both already available there.

### Scope of the deletion

Removed: the producer `differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes`, the dispatch arm
`_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch`, `inbound_probe.py` (43 lines — `ProbeBranch`, `ProbeResult`,
`ProbeConfigError`), `route_inbound_probe` + its re-export, `backend.probe_remote` and the
`SupportsAbsenceProbe` capability, and the fixture-only
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_emits_probe.py` (AC #3).

**`drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions` STAYS.** The ticket's "what is NOT the fix" trap applies
to WIRE: the suppression exists because the caller passes the legacy `(prev, curr)` pair, and DELETE
does not change the caller, so the suppression remains exactly as correct as it is today. Removing it
here would un-suppress two unsound arms — the opposite of the trap, and just as wrong.

`_apply_inbound_delete` and its `typed_dispatch` entry are **kept**, orphaned deliberately, with a
comment naming the follow-up. Deleting c244's implementation in the same change would make restoring
same-pass re-create a rewrite rather than a re-wire.

comments.body:
## DECISION-3B5F-B: REVISED — **re-home, not wire-or-delete**. Symmetry is not a defence.

The operator's correction: *"If Cloud and DC both fail to implement functionality necessary for sync
with their respective ticket systems, they are both deficient."* That is right, and DECISION-3B5F-A
leaned on symmetry as though it were exculpatory. It is not — it is two deficiencies, not zero. The
question is not "is this DC-specific?" but "is this functionality necessary?"

### What is genuinely missing, measured

Necessary and PRESENT: the deletion-vs-aged-out discrimination. Two live implementations
(`outbound_differ._safe_get_issue`, `binding_walk.py:187-196`), and verified live on real DC —
`test_a_deleted_dc_issue_never_plans_a_local_teardown` **PASSED** in harness run 30933704255.

Missing: c244's **same-pass** re-creation of a hard-deleted issue whose local ticket still exists.

I claimed in DECISION-3B5F-A that the outcome still happens "eventually" and did not test it. Tested
now, against a real `BindingStore`:

    bind_confirm(local-1, DIG-1)      -> get_jira_key = 'DIG-1'  is_bound = True
    note_absent #1 (confirmed 404)    -> 'DIG-1'
    note_absent #2                    -> 'DIG-1'
    note_absent #3                    -> None      <-- retired at grace
    FINAL                             -> get_jira_key = None, is_bound = False

`_retire` (`binding_store.py:564-577`) pops the entry from BOTH `bindings` and `reverse`, so the local
ticket is genuinely unbound, and `outbound_differ.py:502-513` then emits the outbound CREATE for it.
So the claim holds — but it is a **latency** deficiency (3 passes instead of 1), not a lost capability.

### Why that still leaves us deficient, and why DELETE-as-written was the wrong call

Three passes of delay is a real regression against a documented guarantee, and ADR 0028's Consequences
assert the same-pass behaviour as a CLOSED gap: *"Confirmed hard-delete of a still-locally-present
ticket now re-creates it (c244) … This closes the former `epic-3e36` gap where the follow-on was built
but never consumed."* The follow-on is, again, never consumed. **The ADR is currently inaccurate**, and
that is true whichever way this ticket goes.

Deleting the chain and accepting the delay would have made the deficiency permanent and undocumented.
That is what the correction catches.

### The third option the brief did not enumerate

Neither WIRE (migrate the legacy `(prev, curr)` caller) nor DELETE (drop the chain) is right:

* WIRE re-lights the snapshot differ's `field_drift` and `unbound_local` arms
  (`reconcile_helpers.py:505-511`), which now duplicate `outbound_differ` (local↔remote diff) and
  `binding_walk` (drift classes A and B). `binding_walk.py:120-123` states that division of labour
  explicitly. Re-enabling a legacy arm to recover one property while double-emitting two others is a
  bad trade.
* DELETE, per above, makes the deficiency permanent.

**RE-HOME instead: delete the dead legacy arm, and move probe consumption to `binding_walk`, where the
confirmed 404 already exists.** Concretely:

1. `binding_walk` already performs the bounded GET and already knows `CONFIRMED_404`. On that state,
   for a binding whose LOCAL ticket is still present, emit the inbound-delete follow-on so
   `_apply_inbound_delete` (`apply_inbound.py:175`) runs and `create_after_hard_delete`
   (`apply_inbound.py:220`) fires **in the same pass** — restoring c244 without touching the differ.
2. Have `binding_walk` reach the probe through the **backend port** `probe_remote`
   (`SupportsAbsenceProbe`, `_backend.py:508-517`) rather than reaching into another module's private
   `outbound_differ._safe_get_issue`. That fixes a real layering violation AND gives the capability a
   live caller. Both adapters already implement it — Cloud `adapters/jira/backend.py:272`, DC
   `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:440` → `transport.py:213`, the latter classifying through the
   shared `classify_probe_response` bound to configured `resolved_statuses`.
3. Delete the genuinely dead legacy pieces: the producer
   `differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes`, the dispatch arm
   `_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch`, `route_inbound_probe`, and the fixture-only
   `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_emits_probe.py`.
4. KEEP `inbound_probe.py` (`ProbeBranch`/`ProbeResult`) — it becomes the live vocabulary
   `probe_remote` returns and `binding_walk` consumes, not dead code.
5. `drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions` **stays**. The caller is unchanged, so the suppression
   remains exactly as correct as today. (The ticket's "what is NOT the fix" trap is about WIRE; this
   path does not touch the caller.)
6. Correct ADR 0028's Consequences to describe where the same-pass re-create actually lives.

### Scope note

This is materially larger than the deletion I scoped in DECISION-3B5F-A — it touches the hot pass and
restores a destructive-adjacent behaviour — so it needs `file_impact` + `review-plan` before
implementation, and a RED-first test proving `(inbound, delete)` is produced from the REAL production
path (AC #2's requirement, now satisfiable because `binding_walk` IS a real producer).

comments.body:
## DECISION-3B5F-C: prior art INVERTS part of B. Restoring same-pass resurrection may be optimising the wrong behaviour.

Checked the re-home plan against how actively-maintained Jira integrations actually handle this. Three
findings, and the second one contradicts DECISION-3B5F-B's plan.

### 1. Detection channel: the industry uses WEBHOOKS; polling "often misses deletions"

Mature integrations subscribe to Jira's `jira:issue_deleted` event rather than inferring deletion from
a polled working set. Atlassian's own webhook docs and integration guides make the point that polling
catches new and edited issues but deletions "slip through the cracks".

**This does not indict rebar's approach**, and one caveat actively vindicates it: deleting a PROJECT
from the UI does **not** fire issue-deleted webhooks, so even webhook-driven tools need a
reconciliation backstop. rebar is a git-backed CLI with no webhook receiver, so a bounded-GET probe is
the correct shape for its architecture — it is the fallback the webhook tools also need, not a
substitute they avoided.

### 2. Re-creating a deleted item: the leading commercial syncer DELIBERATELY REFUSES TO

Unito, on moved/deleted work items, states plainly that it **will not recreate deleted work items**,
"assuming that once a work item is deleted, you don't want it back", and that this exists specifically
to **prevent flows from creating copies of work items you want to stay deleted**.

That is a considered rejection of exactly what c244 does. Kubernetes-style reconcilers land in the same
place from a different direction: the idiomatic handling of a missing object is `IgnoreNotFound` —
"controllers shouldn't try to determine *why* a resource is missing … simply observe that it's missing"
— never resurrect it.

**So DECISION-3B5F-B was about to restore, faster, a behaviour that the closest commercial analogue
treats as a defect to guard against.** "The ADR promises same-pass re-create and we lost it" is true,
and the right response is not automatically to give it back.

### 3. rebar's DISCRIMINATION is more conservative than Kubernetes — and correctly so

K8s can treat "absent from cache" as gone because the informer cache is *intended* to be complete.
rebar's working set is **deliberately incomplete**: ADR 0028 L17's split-JQL caps the Done window, so
absence is expected for live issues. That asymmetry is exactly why the four-way
`observe_jira` (present / confirmed-404 / absent-in-window / transport-error) is justified where a K8s
controller needs no such thing. This part of the design is *better* than a naive port of the reconciler
pattern, and nothing here argues against it.

### The inversion, stated plainly

rebar today **already resurrects** a hard-deleted issue — just slowly. Measured earlier: 3 consecutive
confirmed 404s retire the binding (`_retire` pops it from `bindings` and `reverse`), the local ticket
becomes unbound, and `outbound_differ.py:502-513` creates a fresh Jira issue. So the "deficiency" of
c244 being dead is **not** that rebar fails to resurrect; it is that rebar resurrects on a 3-pass delay
instead of immediately. Both are the behaviour Unito exists to prevent.

Which makes the real question not "same-pass or eventual?" but **"should a confirmed hard-delete
resurrect at all?"** That is a product decision about whose intent wins — the operator who deleted the
Jira issue, or the local store that still holds the ticket — and it is not answerable from the code.

### Revised recommendation

1. **Delete the dead legacy arm.** Uncontested by all three findings, and unchanged from A and B.
2. **Do NOT restore same-pass resurrection.** Making an arguably-wrong behaviour faster is the worst of
   the available moves.
3. **Escalate the real question:** should a confirmed hard-delete resurrect? Prior art says no by
   default. The likely right shape is an explicit policy — resurrect vs. tombstone-and-stop-syncing —
   defaulting to NOT resurrecting, with the local ticket marked so the divergence is visible rather
   than silently re-created. That is a larger design change than this ticket and wants its own ADR
   amendment, because it also governs the EXISTING eventual-resurrection path, which no ticket has ever
   examined.
4. **Correct ADR 0028 either way.** Its Consequences assert c244 works; it does not. Leaving that
   uncorrected is how the next reader re-derives this from scratch.

### What I am NOT claiming

I have not audited Exalate's or sync2jira's delete semantics at code level, and the searches did not
surface Exalate's specific behaviour — so "the industry" here rests on Unito's documented behaviour
plus the Kubernetes reconciler convention, not on a survey. Treat item 2 as strong evidence, not
settled consensus.

Sources: Unito on moved/deleted work items (guide.unito.io/how-does-moving-work-items-work-with-unito);
Atlassian webhooks (developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/webhooks/,
developer.atlassian.com/server/jira/platform/webhooks/); kubebuilder finalizers
(book.kubebuilder.io/reference/using-finalizers); controller-runtime reconcile
(pkg.go.dev/sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/reconcile).

comments.body:
## CITATION-3B5F-D: the inherited b9b8 claim is HALF right — and so is the review that refuted it

`review-plan` blocked on this, correctly flagging that I had carried an inherited citation without
checking it. Checked now. Both accounts are partly wrong.

**The ticket (and the handoff) said:** "Ticket b9b8 already reworked the live DC cell
`test_a_deleted_dc_issue_is_planned_as_an_inbound_probe` for exactly this reason."

**The reviewer said:** refuted — "b9b8's actual scope is title-mirroring (`outbound_field_diff`)".

**The truth:** `b9b8-1c40-ea53-4ef3` is titled *"inbound title reverted by outbound local-wins"* and
its root cause is `outbound_field_diff.py:38-45` omitting `title` from `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS`. So
the reviewer is right about the ticket's SCOPE. But the rework really did happen, and it really did
ride b9b8's commit:

    commit ae009443a9  "b9b8: mirror a Jira-side title edit inbound"
      tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_dc_mutations.py
      - def test_a_deleted_dc_issue_is_planned_as_an_inbound_probe(
      + def test_a_deleted_dc_issue_never_plans_a_local_teardown(

So the cell WAS renamed and re-oracled, in a commit whose ticket was about something else entirely.
The claim is substantively correct about what happened and wrong about why — it was **bundled into
b9b8's commit, not part of b9b8's scope.** The reviewer's "refuted" overshoots; the ticket's "for
exactly this reason" overclaims.

**Third instance of this pattern in this epic.** 2bc7's fix landed under J4's commit
(`rebar-ticket: 0a94`), which is why 2bc7's close could not find a referencing commit and got forced.
This cell's rework landed under b9b8's. Both times the consequence was the same: the work is real, but
it is not attributable from the ticket, so a later reader either cannot find it or cites the wrong
cause. Worth naming as a recurring cost of bundling, not just as two anecdotes.

The description is corrected to state the bundling precisely. The substantive point the citation was
supporting — that the cell no longer asserts an `(inbound, probe)` observable, because no production
path emits one — is unaffected and independently verified: the current cell asserts the ADR 0028 §1
teardown observable and PASSED live in harness run 30933704255.

## IMPLEMENTATION NOTE — RED->GREEN + mutation check recorded

Implemented in worktree `3b5f-tombstone` (off `origin/main` @ f374062ac9).

**RED (before the guard, run explicitly):** the new module
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_no_resurrection_after_confirmed_delete_3b5f.py`
failed 6 / passed 3 —
`test_a_retired_pairing_gets_no_outbound_create` failed with 'A local ticket whose
binding was retired on a confirmed 404 must NOT be re-created in Jira', which is the
resurrection the operator ruling forbids, reproduced from a REAL `BindingStore` driven to
retirement the production way (3x confirmed-404 `note_absent`, not by hand-writing
`bindings-retired.json`). `unretire` / `is_retired_local` failed with AttributeError.
**GREEN after:** 9/9.

**Mutation check of the guard:** with the 4-line guard in
`_compute_outbound_create_mutation` reverted and everything else intact, exactly the 3
behavioural cells re-failed (no-create, never-bound-still-creates, observability); the
fail-open/legacy-tolerance and WIRE-trap cells stayed green, which is correct — they do not
depend on the guard. Guard restored, 9/9.

Notable implementation choices:
* `is_retired_local(local_id) -> bool` is implemented on top of a
  `retired_key_for_local(local_id) -> str | None` primitive, because the suppression
  message has to NAME the retired key and `unretire(<key>)`. Both are public.
* The observable is a deduped bridge alert `outbound-create-suppressed` (the same channel
  `binding-retired` uses), carrying local_id, jira_key, reason and
  `remedy: BindingStore.unretire('<key>')`.
* `outbound_differ.py` sits at the LOCKED module-size cap: the guard's lines were bought
  back by generalizing `_best_effort` to RETURN the member's value and re-expressing
  `_is_retired` on top of it (the void call sites ignore the return). Final size 798/800.
* Step B also removed `reconcile_helpers._audit_log_probe` and its `reconcile.py`
  re-export — it was `route_inbound_probe`'s private stderr helper and had no other
  caller, so leaving it would be the same orphaning the reviewer blocked for
  `_apply_inbound_delete`.
* Step C additionally removed `_build_hard_delete_recreate` and the
  `pending_hard_delete_creates` plumbing in `applier.apply()` — that IS the
  `create_after_hard_delete` consumption, so removing only the call site would have
  orphaned the builder.
* Dormant port recorded in code (`inbound_probe.py` module docstring +
  `SupportsAbsenceProbe` docstring) and in ADR 0028, both naming epic e369 AC5 as the
  reason it is not removed. Follow-up: f020-0960-2c42-4d61 (mega-glaciered-mongrel),
  linked `discovered_from` 3b5f.
* B1 respected: `probe_remote` / `SupportsAbsenceProbe` / `inbound_probe.py` and BOTH
  adapter implementations are untouched. D respected:
  `drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions` is present, still called at
  `run_differs.py`, and pinned by a test so the WIRE trap cannot be entered by accident.

comments.body:
## HANDOFF-3B5F: implementation delegated to a subagent; plan is attested, do not redesign it

State: `in_progress`, claimed. Plan-review verdict **PASS, signed**. A subagent is implementing steps
A0/A/B/B1/C/D/E from the description. No code had been written at handoff time.

**The decision is settled — read DECISION-3B5F-C before touching anything.** It is *re-home*, not the
wire-or-delete the brief offered:

* the deletion discrimination is already live twice (`outbound_differ._safe_get_issue`,
  `binding_walk.py:187-196`), verified on real DC (Row 14 PASSED, run 30933704255);
* prior art rejects resurrection — Unito will not re-create deleted work items, deliberately; Kubernetes
  reconcilers `IgnoreNotFound` and never resurrect;
* so under the operator's ruling ("once deleted in Jira, never resurrected") the resurrection
  IMPLEMENTATION is removed rather than orphaned, AND a tombstone guard stops the EXISTING
  eventual-resurrection path.

**Measured, so it does not need re-deriving:** 3 consecutive confirmed-404 `note_absent` calls retire the
binding; `_retire` (`binding_store.py:564-577`) pops it from BOTH `bindings` and `reverse`;
`get_jira_key` then returns `None`; and `outbound_differ.py:502-513` creates a fresh Jira issue for any
unbound local ticket. That is the resurrection to stop.

**Three traps, each already cost someone something:**
1. `drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions` STAYS — the caller is unchanged, so it remains correct.
   The ticket's "what is NOT the fix" warning is about the WIRE option, which is not being taken.
2. The port capability (`probe_remote`, `SupportsAbsenceProbe`, `inbound_probe.py`) STAYS — removing
   DC's `probe_remote` drops DC's only import of the shared `classify_probe_response`, leaving it
   Cloud-only and weakening epic e369's AC5. Reasoned exclusion, recorded as plan step B1.
3. Engine modules load BY FILENAME STRING through a dynamic loader. For every symbol removed, ALSO grep
   the name as a string — an import-graph check alone misses the call site.

Verify the subagent's work against the ACs before closing; do not close on its report alone.

Subagent implemented the attested plan. Change **1393** (`72e7988419`, branch `3b5f-tombstone`, worktree

### Reported evidence (subagent's, not independently re-run by me)

* **RED-first**: 6 failed / 3 passed before implementation, 9/9 after. The load-bearing red reproduced the

* **Mutation check**: reverting ONLY the 4-line guard in `_compute_outbound_create_mutation` re-failed
  exactly the three behavioural cells (no-create, never-bound-still-creates, observability) while the
  fail-open and WIRE-trap cells stayed green — correct, they do not depend on the guard.
* Gates: `make lint`, `make typecheck` (432 files), `pytest tests/unit` **8035 passed / 28 skipped / 0
  failed**. `outbound_differ.py` is 798/800 — verified independently.
* All three traps respected: the suppression stays and is pinned by a test; the port capability
  (`probe_remote` / `SupportsAbsenceProbe` / `inbound_probe.py` / both adapter impls) is untouched with
  follow-up [rebar:f020-0960-2c42-4d61] filed; symbol removals were grep-checked as strings.

### The judgement calls a reviewer should look at FIRST

The subagent flagged these itself, which is the right instinct — none is obviously wrong, none is
obviously fine:

1. **Scope creep that is arguably correct**: it also removed `reconcile_helpers._audit_log_probe`,
   `_build_hard_delete_recreate` and the `pending_hard_delete_creates` plumbing, on the reasoning that
   removing only the call sites would orphan the builders — the exact objection `review-plan` raised
   against leaving `_apply_inbound_delete` behind. Consistent with the plan's intent; wider than its
   literal text.
2. **`mutation._VALID_COMBINATIONS` still permits `(inbound, delete)` / `(inbound, probe)`.** Only the
   leaves and dispatch entries are gone, so such a mutation would now raise `UnknownActionError` rather
   than being rejected up front. Deliberately left because the plan did not ask to narrow the allowlist
   and the existing tests assert `_LEAVES ⊆ _VALID_COMBINATIONS`, not the reverse. Defensible, but it is
   a loose end someone should agree to.
3. **`docs/env-vars.md` changed** — one file beyond the declared `file_impact`. It is generated and gated
   by `test_gen_env_registry.py`; removing `_apply_inbound_delete` shifted an `os.environ.get(<non-literal>)`

   this change rather than pre-existing.
4. `is_retired_local` is built on a new `retired_key_for_local(local_id) -> str | None` primitive so the
   suppression message can NAME the retired key and `unretire(<key>)`. Both public; the plan's signature
   is honoured.

**Do not close 3b5f on this report.** Verify against the acceptance criteria and wait for both Gerrit
gates — a passing local suite is not `Verified +1`.

# The `(inbound, probe)` dispatch chain is a documented subsystem with no live producer

## Status

DISCOVERED while fixing d103-c3f8-2fbc-4c97 / 727f-b351-59ba-4b3b. Not a regression those
fixes introduced - it predates them and neither changes it. Filed so it is not lost.

## What is unreachable

`differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes` is the only producer of
`(inbound, probe)` mutations. It iterates `local_state` looking for entries carrying a
bound `jira_key` field. Its sole production caller, `run_differs`, passes
`prev_snapshot` - a FETCHED Jira snapshot, whose entries never carry `jira_key`
(`fetcher.py`, and the contract shape in `_snapshot_schema.py`). The loop therefore never
emits, and everything downstream of it is dead in production:

* `_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch` in `run_differs.py`
* `inbound_probe.py` (`ProbeResult`, `ProbeBranch`)
* the router `route_inbound_probe` — which lives in `reconcile_helpers.py` and is re-exported at
  `reconcile.py:66`, NOT in `inbound_probe.py` as an earlier draft of this section claimed
* `backend.probe_remote` / the `SupportsAbsenceProbe` capability

Confirmed empirically: fed a realistic fetched-snapshot pair, `compute_mutations` emits only
`jira_new`, `unbound_local` and `field_drift`. The only fixture in the repo that supplies a
`jira_key`-bearing `local_state` is
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_emits_probe.py`.

## Why it matters

This is the mechanism ADR 0028 para 2 relies on to tell "deleted" from "aged out of the fetch
window" - deletion is proven only by a bounded direct GET returning 404. With no live producer,
that discrimination is never exercised in production.

The live DC cell that once asserted the probe WAS re-oracled, but the inherited wording for it was
wrong and is corrected here (see CITATION-3B5F-D). The rename
`test_a_deleted_dc_issue_is_planned_as_an_inbound_probe` ->
`test_a_deleted_dc_issue_never_plans_a_local_teardown` landed in commit `ae009443a9`, whose subject is
`b9b8: mirror a Jira-side title edit inbound`. It was BUNDLED INTO b9b8's commit, not part of b9b8's
scope (b9b8 is a title-mirroring bug in `outbound_field_diff.py:38-45`). The cell today asserts the
ADR 0028 para 1 observable and PASSED live in harness run 30933704255.

## What is NOT the fix

Do NOT re-enable the arm by making `run_differs` pass a `jira_key`-bearing local_state without
also removing `reconcile_helpers.drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions` in the SAME change.
That suppression exists only because the caller passes the legacy `(prev, curr)` pair; migrating
the caller makes the suppressed emissions correct again, and leaving both in place would silently
drop real work.

## OPERATOR RULING (2026-08-04): once an issue is deleted in Jira, it shouldn't be resurrected.

This settles the question DECISION-3B5F-C escalated, and it widens the ticket: rebar resurrects TODAY,
on a delay, through a path no ticket has examined.

**Measured, not assumed** (real `BindingStore`): 3 consecutive confirmed-404 `note_absent` calls retire
the binding; `_retire` (`binding_store.py:564-577`) pops the entry from BOTH `bindings` and `reverse`;
`get_jira_key` then returns `None`, so the local ticket is UNBOUND; and `outbound_differ.py:502-513`
emits an outbound CREATE for any unbound local ticket. A fresh Jira issue therefore replaces the
deliberately-deleted one about 3 passes later.

Prior art agrees with the ruling: Unito will not recreate deleted work items, "assuming that once a
work item is deleted, you don't want it back", explicitly to stop flows re-creating things you wanted
gone; Kubernetes reconcilers treat a missing object with `IgnoreNotFound` and never resurrect.

**`is_retired` does not prevent this.** It exists (`binding_store.py:612`) and is consulted at
`outbound_differ.py:590`, but only to keep retired keys OUT of the GET-probe candidate list. It is
keyed by `jira_key`, and the unbound-create arm has no retired check at all.

## Plan

**A0. Define the escape hatch - it does not exist yet.** There is NO un-retire API: `is_retired` reads
(`binding_store.py:612`), `clear_absent` only resets the 404 counter (`:589`), and `_retire` (`:564`) is
private and one-way. A tombstone would be permanent with no route out but hand-editing
`.bridge_state/bindings-retired.json`. So this adds `BindingStore.unretire(jira_key)`: drop the key
from the retired set and file so the next pass treats the ticket as ordinary unbound work. The
suppression message names this call.

**A. Tombstone a confirmed-deleted pairing so it is never re-created.**
1. Add `BindingStore.is_retired_local(local_id) -> bool` - a reverse lookup over the retired entries
   (`bindings-retired.json` is keyed by `jira_key` and carries `local_id`, so only the accessor is
   missing). Same duck-typed/fail-open tolerance as `outbound_differ._is_retired`.
2. Guard the unbound-create arm at `outbound_differ.py:510-513`: a local ticket with NO live binding
   but WITH a retired one was previously paired with a remote that returned a confirmed 404 - skip the
   create. A never-bound ticket still creates normally; that distinction is the whole point.
3. Make it VISIBLE: a bridge alert / sync-log line naming the local id and the retired key, and naming
   `unretire` as the route back.

**B. Delete the dead legacy probe arm:** the producer
`differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes`, the dispatch arm
`_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch`, `route_inbound_probe` (`reconcile_helpers.py`) and its
re-export at `reconcile.py:66`.

**B2. THE CONSUMER INVENTORY — every module that exercises a removed symbol.** A prior revision of
this plan named only the fixture-only test, which under-declared the blast radius: eight further
modules reference these symbols directly and would break unaddressed. `review-plan` blocked on
exactly that, correctly. The complete set, and the disposition of each:

*Deleted* (the module's whole subject is the removed chain):
* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_emits_probe.py` — the only fixture supplying a
  `jira_key`-bearing `local_state`, i.e. a synthetic input the real caller never produces
* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_inbound_probe_dispatch.py` — exercises
  `route_inbound_probe` across all branches

*Updated* (the module has a legitimate wider subject; only the dead-chain assertions go, and a
comment records the removal so the next reader is not left guessing):
* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability.py` — called
  `_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch` directly
* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability_heldout.py` — likewise
* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_snapshot_differ_stale_local_state.py` — asserted the
  dispatch as a stubbed phase

Source modules carrying the removals besides the four named above: `reconcile.py` (re-export),
`typed_dispatch.py`, `applier.py`, `apply_inbound.py`, `_backend.py`, `inbound_probe.py` (dormancy
note only).

**B1. SCOPE BOUNDARY - the port capability stays, as a reasoned exclusion.** `inbound_probe.py`,
`backend.probe_remote` and `SupportsAbsenceProbe` also lose their only consumer, but removing DC's
`probe_remote` (`adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py:213-229`) removes DC's only import of the shared
`classify_probe_response`, leaving it used by Cloud alone (`adapters/jira/probe.py:85,98,100`) - which
weakens **epic e369 AC5**, whose claim is that the probe classifier has one implementation in
`jira_family` imported by BOTH backends. Trading an epic-level AC to delete a dormant Protocol is a
separate decision; recorded as dormant with a follow-up.

**C. Do NOT restore same-pass re-create - and REMOVE its implementation rather than orphaning it.**
An earlier draft kept `_apply_inbound_delete` "for a possible re-wire"; `review-plan` blocked that as
leaving a removed producer's consumer behind, and under the ruling the objection is stronger than the
reviewer put it: `create_after_hard_delete` (`apply_inbound.py:220`) is not merely unreachable, it is
now UNWANTED - it IS the resurrection ruled against. So the leaf goes: `_apply_inbound_delete`
(`apply_inbound.py:175-284`), its `("inbound","delete")` entry (`typed_dispatch.py:92`), the
`_apply_inbound_probe` marker leaf and its `applier.py` registration, and the
`create_after_hard_delete` consumption at `applier.py:452`. No half-wired resurrection path remains.

**C1. Plan C's consumer inventory.** Removing the leaf orphans its builders, so they go too:
`_build_hard_delete_recreate` and the `pending_hard_delete_creates` plumbing, plus
`reconcile_helpers._audit_log_probe`. Test consumers:

*Deleted*: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_hard_delete_recreate.py` — its entire subject is
the same-pass re-create this ruling forbids.

*Updated*: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_inbound_leaf_bodies.py` (asserted
`create_after_hard_delete`) and `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate/test_leaves_effect_matrix.py`
(asserted the `(inbound,probe)` marker leaf via `_drive_inbound_probe`).

*Updated (a THIRD guard, found by CI not by my grep)*:
`tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_post_deletion_linkage.py` pins the exact
`(direction, action)` pairs as a LITERAL `EXPECTED_LEAF_PAIRS` frozenset, so removing the two
inbound leaves is registry DRIFT to it. The two pairs are dropped from that pinned set with the
reason recorded inline; the guard still pins the remaining pairs, so an ACCIDENTAL drop still
fails. It was missed locally because the file lives under `tests/integration/` but is NOT marked
`integration`, and CI selects by MARKER (`pytest -m "not integration and not external"`) — so a
path-based local run (`pytest tests/unit`) cannot see it. Reproduce with the marker selection.

*Deliberately NOT modified*: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_applier.py` and
`apply/test_applier_direction_guard.py` iterate the `_LEAVES` registry and cross-check it against
`mutation._VALID_COMBINATIONS`. They keep passing unmodified because they assert
`_LEAVES` ⊆ `_VALID_COMBINATIONS`, not the converse. **Known loose end, stated rather than hidden:**
`_VALID_COMBINATIONS` still permits `(inbound, delete)` and `(inbound, probe)`, so such a mutation
would now raise `UnknownActionError` at dispatch rather than being rejected up front. Narrowing the
allowlist is deliberately out of scope here — it would change a shared validation contract this
ticket did not review — and it is recorded so a reviewer agrees to it rather than discovers it.

**D. `drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions` STAYS.** The caller is unchanged, so the suppression
is exactly as correct as today. (The "what is NOT the fix" trap applies to the WIRE option, not taken.)

**E. Correct ADR 0028.** Its Consequences assert c244 re-creates a hard-deleted issue in the same pass.
That is false today and, under this ruling, no longer desired. Replace with tombstone semantics and
note that absence-vs-deletion discrimination lives in `outbound_differ` + `binding_walk`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Establish whether the absence-probe path is still wanted, or whether ADR 0028 para 2's
      direct-GET confirmation has since been implemented elsewhere. **ANSWERED** — implemented twice
      and both live: `outbound_differ._safe_get_issue` (L13) and `binding_walk.py:187-196` (ADR para 4),
      called at `run_differs.py:222` / `:257`. Verified live on DC: Row 14
      `test_a_deleted_dc_issue_never_plans_a_local_teardown` PASSED in harness run 30933704255.
- [x] ~~a RED-first test proving `(inbound, probe)` is produced from the real production call path~~ —
      **MOOT** under the operator ruling; no producer is to be created.
- [ ] the dead chain is removed: `differ._compute_mutations_emit_absent_partner_probes`,
      `_run_differs_inbound_probe_dispatch`, `route_inbound_probe`, and the fixture-only
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_differ_emits_probe.py`
- [ ] RED-first: a local ticket whose binding was retired on a confirmed 404 gets NO outbound create —
      the test FAILS before the guard exists and PASSES after, checked by running it at both commits
- [ ] a never-bound local ticket STILL gets its outbound create, asserted in the same test module so
      the guard cannot suppress ordinary creation
- [ ] the suppression is observable (bridge alert or sync-log line) naming the local id and the retired
      key, and the message names `BindingStore.unretire(<jira_key>)` as the route to re-enable creation
- [ ] `BindingStore.unretire(jira_key)` exists, drops the key from BOTH the in-memory retired set and
      `bindings-retired.json`, and a test proves the local ticket is created again on the next pass —
      so the tombstone is reversible by a documented call rather than by hand-editing state
- [ ] the dormant port capability (`probe_remote` / `SupportsAbsenceProbe` / `inbound_probe.py`) is
      recorded as dormant with a follow-up ticket, and the reason it is not removed here (epic e369
      AC5's both-backends claim on `classify_probe_response`) is stated
- [ ] `BindingStore.is_retired_local(local_id)` tolerates legacy/duck-typed stores the way
      `outbound_differ._is_retired` does — asserted with a stub store lacking the method
- [ ] the resurrection implementation is removed, not orphaned: `_apply_inbound_delete`, the
      `("inbound","delete")` typed_dispatch entry, the `_apply_inbound_probe` marker leaf, and the
      `create_after_hard_delete` consumption in `applier.py` — verified by the suite passing with them
      gone and a grep showing no remaining reference
- [ ] ADR 0028's c244 Consequence is corrected to describe tombstone semantics
- [ ] `drop_snapshot_differ_local_state_emissions` is still present and still consulted — asserted, so
      the WIRE trap cannot be entered by accident

## Testing

    pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler -q                    # the reconciler tier
    pytest tests/unit -q                                     # full unit suite (no regressions)
    make lint && make typecheck

The RED-first proof for the tombstone guard is run explicitly at two commits: the test is added
first and must FAIL against the pre-guard tree, then PASS once the guard lands. A guard asserted
without a demonstrated RED is unverified, and this one suppresses work — the failure mode of a
wrong guard is silently not creating issues, which no green suite would surface.

Removal of the dead chain is proved by the suite continuing to pass with the producer, the dispatch
arm and the router gone — plus a grep confirming no remaining `(inbound, probe)` producer, since the
dynamic loader means an import-graph check alone would miss a string-loaded module.
